title: README class-color claim unreliable: pooled packet dots keep the first occupant's class material on reuse
evidence:
README.md (chunk c2): "Packets then stream along the arcs: blue dots are streaming, yellow are
email; strand thickness = the lane's share, strand speed = lane priority". scripts/flow_view.gd `_sync_dots` (verified in worktree): "			if used < pool.size():
				dot = pool[used]
				dot.visible = true
			else:
				dot = MeshInstance3D.new()
				...
				dot.material_override = _dot_mats[pkt.cls]" — material_override is assigned ONLY in the creation branch (line 153); the reuse branch (lines 142-144) never reassigns it.
detail: Dot pools persist per pipe across syncs. When a reused slot's packet changes class, the dot keeps the old class color, so blue/yellow class identity breaks under mixed traffic — contradicting the README's player-facing claim.
recommended_fix: Assign dot.material_override = _dot_mats[pkt.cls] on every use (hoist line 153 out of the else branch), or maintain per-class dot pools.

title: Stale cross-reference: test_gesture.gd header still cites test_no_sim, which this diff renames to test_world
evidence: tests/test_gesture.gd:6 (verbatim, worktree): "## connect_programmatic shortcut (that path is covered in test_no_sim)." The c2 diff renames the referenced file: "diff --git a/tests/test_no_sim.gd b/tests/test_world.gd" and run_tests.gd swaps "-\"res://tests/test_no_sim.gd\"," for "+\"res://tests/test_world.gd\",".
detail: The rename (sanctioned by the spec) leaves a dangling pointer in a file this diff edits; future readers tracing programmatic-path coverage hit a nonexistent test.
recommended_fix: Update the test_gesture.gd header comment to reference test_world.gd.
